sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State-respondent.
By means of the instant bail application, the applicant seeks bail in respect of Case Crime No. 27 of 2024 under Sections 498A/304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Reusa, District Sitapur.
The submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that there is no material worth its name to implicate the applicant.
It is pointed out that the applicant has been framed as per the version of the prosecution.
Lavlesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

It is alleged that the deceased was the wife of the co-accused Vikas Kumar.
It is also alleged that Sri Vikas Kumar used to mate out cruelty to the deceased for want of adequate dowry.

It is also stated that the co-accused had dropped his wife to her own home and and it was also stated that on 16.01.2024, the co-accused and the applicant are said to have killed the victim and thereafter hung her body by a tree.
It is alleged that the name of the applicant has surfaced from the statement of the husband of victim Vikas Kumar, a copy of which has been brought on record as Annexure No.6.

It is further submitted that merely because the applicant was the friend of the co-accused, he has been roped in whereas there is no material to indicate the complicity of the applicant in the alleged crime.

It has further been submitted that the applicant does not have any criminal history and he is languishing in Jail since 20. 01.2024, moreover, the manner in which the incident is said to have occurred does not give credence as there is no involvement of the applicant and the presence of the applicant has not been ascertained and is doubtful and in the aforesaid circumstances, it is urged that the applicant is innocent and be granted bail.

Learned A.G.A. on the basis of material available with him in shape of case diary has opposed the prayer for bail, however, could not dispute the aforesaid fact that in so far as the present applicant is concerned neither his presence has been confirmed nor there is any material collected to indicate that the applicant had any complicity in the aforesaid crime.

Considering the rival submissions, the facts and circumstances of the case and the material available on record as well as considering the nature of allegations and accusation against the applicant, the severity of the punishment if convicted and the period of incarceration as well as the fact that no apprehension has been expressed by the learned AGA that the applicant is at the risk of fleeing justice or that he would tamper with evidence or influence any witness, hence, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Let the applicant Lavlesh Kumar involved in Case Crime No. 27 of 2024 under Sections 498A/304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Reusa, District Sitapur be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two reliable sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
At the time of executing required sureties the following conditions shall be imposed in the interest of justice.
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

In case of default of this condition,
it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed Lavlesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

2 against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i)
opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the trial court, absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Order Date :- 12.4.2024
